leo_support: Customer (Acme Corp) opened a ticket — intermittently getting 429s and occasional 401s when hitting model 'rwd-large-extended' during a load test. They say spikes happen only when sending ~64k context payloads.

maria_g: do we have their repro? request pattern?

leo_support: They shared a short repro curl that sends 5 parallel requests with ~32k tokens each, repeated in a loop. They also recently switched billing plans per their comment. Attaching snippet they provided below.

leo_support: ```bash
for i in {1..5}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-large-extended","input":"<~32k-token-payload>","max_tokens":512}' &
done
wait
```

ops-bot: automated alert: 2025-11-12T16:21:32Z customer=acme-corp region=us-west-2 model=rwd-large-extended 429_count=37 401_count=3 avg_latency_ms=420 max_concurrency=28

jin_park: initial hypothesis: this looks like a combo of per-model RPM/TPM caps + concurrency-based queueing. long contexts increase token processing time so their per-second throughput drops while they still count against RPM/TPM. When a burst arrives it can overflow the per-model token budget and we return 429s. 401s could be short-lived token auth refresh failures on their side after plan change.

maria_g: can you pull the per-model quota/usage for their org id across the window? need RPM, TPM, and concurrency watermark. Also check if we served fallback variants due to kernel selection.

leo_support: pulled logs (excerpt):
```
[1748001234] org=acme id=req_9a2 model=rwd-large-extended tokens_in=32000 tokens_out=512 status=429 reason=token_quota_exhausted
[1748001238] org=acme id=req_9b3 model=rwd-large-extended tokens_in=32000 tokens_out=512 status=429 reason=concurrency_queue_timeout
[1748001241] org=acme id=req_9c1 model=rwd-small status=200 latency_ms=220
[1748001250] org=acme id=req_9d4 status=401 reason=auth_token_revoked
```

maria_g: thanks — that log line matches token_quota_exhausted. Important distinction: RPM/TPM on a per-model basis counts incoming tokens (TPM) and requests (RPM). For long contexts each request uses many tokens so TPM is the limiter. Also note we cap model concurrency (per-org) to 24 for rwd-large-extended in us-west-2 by default.

jin_park: recommended repro to confirm: run 1) single-threaded long-context requests at low rate until TPM spike, 2) run 5 parallel short-context requests to verify concurrency limit behavior. I'll drop a small python script for controlled repro.

jin_park: ```python
# repro.py: controlled spike vs concurrency
import requests, time, threading
URL='https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
HEAD={'Authorization':'Bearer TOKEN','Content-Type':'application/json'}
PAYLOAD={'model':'rwd-large-extended','input':'X'*32000,'max_tokens':64}

def send():
    r=requests.post(URL, json=PAYLOAD, headers=HEAD)
    print(r.status_code, r.text[:120])

# spawn N threads
threads=[threading.Thread(target=send) for _ in range(5)]
for t in threads: t.start()
for t in threads: t.join()
```

leo_support: customer reported the 401s around the same time they changed payment method — billing_bot can you confirm plan change impacts?

billing_bot: noticed invoice/payment event for org=acme at 2025-11-12T16:19:02Z. Payment method updated; subscription temporarily entered a 'pending' state while payment validated — during that window tokens requests returned 401 for ~90s until the payment cleared. No billing overages.

maria_g: OK that explains 401s. For 429s: we should educate them: long-context workloads need token-budget planning. Short-term mitigations: 1) reduce context size or chunk into multiple calls, 2) switch to rwd-large-medium (lower concurrency but lower TPM footprint) or use the 'streaming' option to reduce buffer, 3) implement exponential backoff with jitter (we have 429 Retry-After semantics).

leo_support: I suggested immediate tactical steps to customer: add exponential backoff (start 500ms, backoff x2, jitter), reduce parallelism to <=12 for rwd-large-extended in us-west-2, and try temporary model downgrade to rwd-medium-extended. Also asked for a small repro run of the python script.

jin_park: long-term: we should check whether their traffic pattern needs a dedicated capacity slot (Reserved/Dedicated) — because sustained long-context high-TPM workloads are exactly what Dedicated is for. I'll tag infra for capacity guidance.

maria_g: logging action items: 1) confirm per-model RPM/TPM windows for acme for 16:18–16:26 (leo), 2) share recommended backoff snippet and our token-counting doc to customer (leo), 3) recommend Dedicated if they plan sustained >X TPM (jin to prepare numbers).

leo_support: customer accepted repro request, will run script and report back. Closing note: we should add FAQ blurb about "billing transition causes transient 401s" and another about "long-context -> TPM exhaustion" in support docs.

ops-bot: note: follow-up alert suppressed until next business hour, case_status=waiting_on_customer
